en: The Panama Canal uses lock systems, which function as massive water-filled inclined planes to lift ships.
The rough skin of a shark reduces water friction, allowing it to swim through the ocean faster.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa remains standing because its center of gravity stays directly above its base.
The homing pigeon uses the Earth's magnetic field to navigate and find its way during long flights.
Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile in 1800, which was the very first electrical battery in history.
The Aurora Borealis produces colorful lights when charged particles from the Sun collide with gases in the atmosphere.
The sperm whale produces the loudest biological sound on Earth, reaching up to 230 decibels underwater.
The hot springs in Tiwi, Albay, are heated by geothermal energy from magma beneath the Earth's crust.
The Malampaya gas platform converts the chemical potential energy of natural gas into electrical energy for Luzon.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft continues moving through space without engines because of inertia in the vacuum of space.
The Golden Gate Bridge uses massive steel cables under tension to support the heavy weight of the roadway.
Solar panels at the Batangas Solar Power Plant convert light energy from the Sun directly into electrical energy.
